Cloud SQL provides managed relational databases; Spanner provides horizontally scalable relational semantics and synchronous replication. Spanner is justified by scale and availability requirements, not by a desire to avoid schema design.

In a production system, cloud SQL needs connection pooling, query tuning, replicas, backups, and failover drills. Spanner needs good primary-key distribution, transaction awareness, instance sizing, and latency measurement across regions. At senior depth, I would quantify the relevant latency, scale, correctness, security, and cost limits, compare the simplest credible alternative, and name the measured threshold that would change the design. For example, account billing stays on regional Cloud SQL, while a truly global ledger with strict consistency and proven scale uses Spanner. I would prove the explanation by showing one expected Cloud SQL and Spanner behavior and one boundary case, then connecting both to observable evidence
